ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver (no fake arrival confirmation was recorded — F6), and remind the driver that a valid no-show fee requires the "I'm Here" tap or a platform-recorded arrival.
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled (F4), so the $6.61 cancellation fee can only be charged through the no-show branch: cancelled_by = driver with a no-show claim routes to NS-1 [F4][NS-0]. The trace settles the three NS-1 elements as failed: no arrival confirmation was recorded (driver_pressed_here_at null; neither tap nor platform auto-arrival) [F6][NS-1], and because that confirmation never occurred, the "within 200 m at the moment of confirmation" element and the "more than 3 minutes at the pickup after confirmation until cancelling" element have no anchor at all — the measurement is 0 s [F6][NS-1]. The driver's own post-trip statement confirms the omission ("I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there"), but a statement made after the event cannot manufacture the missing system record, and the button is not a formality the GPS can cure: the button press is what starts both the arrival and the waiting clock [F12][F6][NS-1].

Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) do not all hold, NS-2 applies and the fee must be refunded in full [F6][F7][NS-2]. The amount follows from the fare record's cancellation fee of $6.61 with no surge (1.0×), and the trace fixes the recoverable sum as the cancellation fee itself: $6.61 [F7][F8][NS-0]. I note that the driver's physical conduct was not blameworthy — he was 34 m away at closest approach, spent 5 min 20 s inside 200 m, and stood stationary 4 min 0 s at 40 m until cancelling [F1][F2][F3] — but on the policy text the delay or unreached pickup does not rescue a fee whose first condition is unrecorded [F3][NS-1]. The trace also marks NS-2's flag_account limb as not triggered: there was no fake confirmation (the record shows no confirmation at all), so no account action against this driver [F6][NS-2].

Profiles are not used to decide the fee: the long, clean histories on both sides (rider 4.9 / 0 upheld; driver 4.87 with 951 trips / 0 upheld) bear only on account action, which is not warranted here [F16][F17][NS-2]. The record is complete on the elements this ruling needs — full timestamped chat, GPS coverage through the cancellation moment, and a fare record — so no escalation for missing evidence is required [F11][F3][F7].

The 4 min 0 s stationary period at 40 m [F3] cannot satisfy NS-1(iii), because that clock runs only after the arrival confirmation, which never occurred (0 s measured) [F6][NS-1].

Elapsed time from acceptance to cancellation (9 min 50 s) [F4] is not an NS-1 element; NS-1 conditions on the recorded arrival confirmation, and the rider's complaint wording ('on my way down') is not contradicted by any system record of her position [F6][NS-1].
Non-confrontational chat and a complete timestamped record [F9][F10][F11] cure no missing record; the fee turns on the arrival confirmation absent in F6, not on the driver's tone [NS-1].

The GPS/timeline records do settle presence but not NS-1(i); a post-hoc statement admitting a forgotten button [F12] cannot create the missing system record, and NS-2 applies once any NS-1 condition fails [F6][NS-1][NS-2].
Clean account histories [F16][F17] do not bear on the fee question; profile facts cannot decide a case alone and cannot cure the failed NS-1(i) record [F6][NS-2].
No safety issue is alleged, but the absence of one does not defeat the fee refund: the case turns on NS-1/NS-2, not on SAFE-1 [F9][F10][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's assertion that she was not a no-show in substance is not established by any rider-side record, and in any event does not drive the outcome: the refund rests on the missing NS-1(i) record [F6][F2][NS-1].
The rider's and driver's profile histories [F16][F17] are not a ground for the refund; profile facts cannot decide the case, and no account action is warranted here [NS-2].
